No Result View All Result Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us Hausa Edition Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Arewa Group Hails Tinubu Over University Reforms, Student Loans by Nonye Ekwenugo 3 minutes ago in News Share on WhatsApp Share on Facebook Share on X Telegram The Arewa Think Tank has commended President Bola Tinubu’s administration for its interventions in the education sector, particularly the establishment of the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) and efforts to restore industrial harmony in universities.
The group’s Convener, Muhammad Alhaji Yakubu, gave the commendation while reacting to an address delivered by the Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of the Governing Council of the University of Ibadan, Chief Adebisi Akande, at the institution’s 78th Foundation Day celebration on Tuesday, 17 November 2026.
Yakubu described Akande’s address as a timely reflection on the challenges facing Nigeria’s higher education system, particularly the need for economic stability, sustainable university funding and improved institutional governance.
He said the Federal Government’s efforts to address disagreements with university-based unions and improve the conditions of service of academic staff were important steps towards stabilising the university system.
According to him, adequately funded and stable universities are essential to national development because of their roles in research, innovation and professional development.
Yakubu particularly described NELFUND as a significant intervention capable of expanding access to higher education, especially for students from financially disadvantaged backgrounds.
He recalled that Akande, in his Foundation Day address, disclosed that NELFUND had processed nearly 2 million student applications and disbursed approximately ₦400 billion to hundreds of tertiary institutions.
Yakubu said the initiative would help reduce the financial barriers preventing qualified Nigerians from accessing higher education.
He urged the Federal Government to sustain and strengthen the scheme, stressing that access to education should not be determined by a student’s financial circumstances.
The Arewa Think Tank convener also supported Akande’s position on the need to end prolonged industrial disputes and disruptions to academic calendars, which he said had affected students, parents and the international competitiveness of Nigerian universities.
He called on the Federal Government, university authorities and academic unions to sustain dialogue, honour agreements and prioritise the future of students.
